reuse.why: The change reuses budget writes, sheet access, month utilities and undo wrappers, but expands repeated category-selection logic instead of sharing it.

duplication.why: Five actions repeat the eligibility query, while copyPreviousMonth implements the same exclusions separately in JavaScript.

placement.why: Budget decisions remain in actions.ts and method registration follows the existing app.ts layering.

scope.why: All edits concern the requested month-wide actions, their registration and focused tests.

maintainability.why: Future eligibility changes require coordinating six implementations across SQL and JavaScript, making policy divergence likely.

bypasses_abstraction.where: The existing tree has no shared month-wide eligibility abstraction, and the change uses the existing mutation and undo abstractions.

disguised_duplication.where: actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth expresses the hidden, fixed-group and saved-template exclusions as JavaScript guards, duplicating the SQL predicates in the other five month-wide actions.

abstraction_drift.where: No shared eligibility helper is introduced or expanded; the design problem is duplicated policy rather than drift of a shared abstraction.
